title: Lowrider Culture in the American Southwest / Cultura Lowrider en el suroeste estadounidense FREE Opening
location: Moab Museum, 118 E. Center St., Moab, UT 84532
description: The Museum is excited to announce our upcoming exhibition, Lowrider Culture in the American Southwest. Presented in collaboration with the National Hispanic Cultural Center and renowned artists, the exhibition opens with a special presentation by Art Limon, founder of the Los Angeles Lowrider Alliance. From 4-7 pm, guests can celebrate lowrider culture with food, music, and complimentary Museum admission. Members of Duke’s Car Club of Salt Lake City, UT and other local participants will showcase their vehicles along Center Street. In the words of Limon, we are excited to present this exhibition here and now “because the moment has arrived when people are finally ready to understand the culture, not just the cars.” Emerging from Mexican American communities in the 1940s, lowriding is a vibrant expression of Chicano identity, blending artistry, engineering, and community pride. The broader region, including nearby San Juan County, has a long history of Hispanic influence in cattle driving, with vaqueros working alongside other cowboys to shape the ranching traditions of the American Southwest. Lowrider Culture in the American Southwest highlights this living tradition, connecting the creativity and innovation of lowriders today with the enduring cultural contributions of Hispanic communities in the region. About our Guest Speaker: Art Limon is the proud founder of the Los Angeles Lowrider Alliance, a volunteer Think Tank organization dedicated to preserving and promoting Lowrider culture and Chicano history through education, advocacy, and community engagement. His work has helped bring Lowrider culture into museum spaces, including contributions to the Smithsonian Lowrider Culture in the United States traveling exhibition. A recognized cultural leader, Art has also participated with major organizations to support underserved communities and has been invited to speak at institutions such as the American Alliance of Museums National Conference. Through his leadership, he continues to elevate Lowriding as a powerful expression of Art, identity, and cultural heritage. About the Semiquincentennial: The semiquincentennial is a chance for everyone to feel a part of this major milestone in our nation. We can celebrate courage, liberty, and sacrifice, while also reckoning with difficult truths. By fostering a sense of belonging and coming together with our local communities, we can ensure that Utahns of all ages and backgrounds see themselves in American history. Next up: Buffalo Soldiers Heritage Trail opening July 28th, 2026!

title: Tai Chi with Drew
location: Wellness Collective, 76 S 100 W, Moab, UT 84532
description: Among all forms of physical activity, Tai Chi Ch’uan is perhaps the most accessible, convenient, and economical way to improve both physical health and mental well-being. As Yang Style Tai Chi master Cheng Man-Ching once said, ‘Those who understand the importance of exercise for health will find Tai Chi Ch’uan indispensable.’ While Tai Chi may not be easy to master, consistent practice will yield results. In this class, we will focus on cultivating chi, building endurance and strength, and developing core alignment, all while learning to release tension. Tai Chi training offers many levels of progression. In Yang Style, when practiced correctly, it becomes an aerobic workout, despite minimal movement. Additionally, it serves as a form of meditation. Please wear comfortable clothing. Flat shoes, socks, or bare feet are ideal. Students are encouraged to train at their own pace, and progression will vary from person to person.
